tax.text: She proposes fully funding the IRS to enforce tax laws against wealthy people who evade them.
tax.quote: Fully fund the IRS and empower staff to hold the rich who cut corners accountable.

wages.text: She proposes raising the federal minimum wage and setting industry-wide wage and benefit floors.
wages.quote: End the tipped minimum wage and raise the federal minimum wage to a family-sustaining level that increases annually with the cost of living.

trade.text: She opposes Trump’s tariffs, saying they increase everyday costs for consumers.
trade.quote: Push back against the nonsense Trump Tariffs that are increasing the prices of everyday goods and harming hard-working Americans' ability to afford necessary items.

debt.text: She says she would protect and expand Social Security.
debt.quote: But Courtney has a real plan to: Protect and expand Social Security

housing.text: She proposes converting vacant or abandoned buildings into affordable homes and increasing housing funding.
housing.quote: Repurpose vacant or abandoned buildings, such as warehouses or schools, into safe and secure affordable homes/complexes

schools.text: She proposes increasing federal support for low-income schools and funding for special education.
schools.quote: Increase Title I funding and expand federal support for low-income schools to ensure equity in education regardless of zip code.

safety.text: She supports prevention programs for at-risk youth to reduce pathways into incarceration.
safety.quote: Invest in preventive programs for at-risk youth who have been expelled from school to curb access to activities or behaviors that lead to the prison pipeline

immigration.text: She opposes detention and deportation as defaults and proposes more legal support in immigration court.
immigration.quote: End detention and deportation as a default by investing in housing, legal support, and integration and divesting from private prison contracts.

guns.text: She supports universal background checks and other measures regulating firearms.
guns.quote: Closing the Charleston loophole and passing comprehensive legislation requiring universal background checks, secure storage, ghost gun regulation, and crime gun tracing

abortion.text: She opposes restrictions on abortion and supports access to reproductive care.
abortion.quote: Oppose the dangerous restrictions placed on women's right to choose by ensuring equal and safe access to reproductive care within South Carolina and across the U.S.

health.text: She supports expanding Medicare and Medicare for All to provide guaranteed coverage.
health.quote: Expand Medicare and support Medicare for All to replace private insurance companies and ensure all South Carolinians have guaranteed healthcare coverage.

energy.text: She proposes breaking up energy monopolies and increasing access to more affordable goods.
energy.quote: Break up food and energy monopolies and increase access to more affordable goods for everyday families in GSP

voting.text: She supports mail-in voting, automatic voter registration, and protections against voter purges.
voting.quote: Protect mail-in voting by restoring the Postal Service and replacing partisan appointees who have gutted its capacity, and ensure that absentee ballots are delivered and counted.

tax.text: He supported the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill and highlighted its tax cuts and increased take-home pay.
tax.quote: Additionally, last summer, Republicans voted to deliver the largest tax cut in American history, increasing Americans’ take-home pay by up to $13,300.

wages.text: In House debate, Timmons said he strongly opposed the PRO Act and urged colleagues to vote no.
wages.quote: Mr. TIMMONS. Mr. Chair, I rise today in strong opposition to the PRO Act.

trade.text: He said tariffs raise goods and services costs, warned against retaliation, and favored enforceable trade agreements.
trade.quote: As far as tariffs go, obviously they distort the cost of goods and services.

debt.text: He praised legislation that reduces the deficit while saying it fully protects Social Security and Medicare.
debt.quote: Delivers the largest mandatory spending cut in decades—while fully protecting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.

housing.text: He supported legislation intended to cut red tape and increase housing supply, saying it would help build more homes.
housing.quote: This bipartisan package cuts red tape, modernizes outdated HUD programs, and empowers community lenders so we can build more homes and lower costs.

schools.text: He said school choice empowers states and parents and cosponsored a resolution recognizing National School Choice Week.
schools.quote: Recognizing school choice is an important part of strengthening those systems and ensuring that states and parents are the ones being empowered, not Washington.

safety.text: He opposes efforts to defund police and supports giving law enforcement officers the tools to do their jobs.
safety.quote: I oppose efforts to defund the police and weaken public safety. Criminals should be prosecuted, violent offenders kept off our streets, and our law enforcement officers given the tools and respect they deserve.

immigration.text: He supports finishing the border wall, ending catch-and-release, and deporting criminal undocumented immigrants.
immigration.quote: I supported President Trump’s border wall and will continue fighting to finish it, end catch-and-release policies, stop the flow of fentanyl, and deport criminal illegal immigrants.

guns.text: He says he will defend gun ownership rights and opposes red-flag laws and efforts to disarm gun owners.
guns.quote: I oppose gun grabs, red flag abuses, and any attempt by Washington liberals to disarm law-abiding Americans.

abortion.text: He describes himself as pro-life and supports policies to protect unborn life.
abortion.quote: I am proudly pro-life and believe every life is a gift from God worth protecting.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which addressed eligibility in women’s sports.
gender.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

cannabis.text: He voted against final passage of H.R. 3617, the MORE Act.
cannabis.quote: Roll Call 107 | Bill Number: H. R. 3617

energy.text: He voted to disapprove an EPA rule setting vehicle multi-pollutant emissions standards for model years 2027 and later.
energy.quote: such rule shall have no force or effect.

voting.text: He voted for the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration.
voting.quote: Vote Question: On Passage SAVE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

debt.text: She calls the national debt the greatest threat to U.S. security and says she would support policies to reduce it.
debt.quote: The single greatest threat to our sovereignty and national security is the national debt.
